correctness.rationale: Direct smallest-missing-odd-part counting yields F=G·Theta with G=E(q^4)/E(q). Jacobi and Gauss give F=Psi(-q)R², where R=∏(1+2q^m/(1+q^{2m}))=1+2U. Modulo two U counts odd divisors, so U+U² is the odd-square indicator. This proves the coefficientwise congruence for all nonnegative indices. Inert primes p=5,7 (mod 8) force even p-adic valuations of 8n+1 for any representation; finite CRT densities and divergence of reciprocals of inert primes prove natural density one of eight-divisibility. A separate verifier checked 601 coefficients and direct partitions for n≤22; these finite tests are corroboration only.

value.rationale: A recently introduced weighted excludant statistic now has a complete, explicit modulo-eight coefficient classifier with an arithmetic representation interpretation. Exact nondivisibility by four occurs only at triangular integers, and divisibility by eight holds on a natural-density-one set through an inert-prime obstruction. These are motivated structural consequences not equivalent to a small finite table, arbitrary slice, or routine base-case check.
